summary: Ankita Chakraborty is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Bijoya Goswami (attested 2026). She held an appointment as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society, attested in 2026.

Ankur Barua works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Sikkim Manipal University, and the University of Hong Kong, he studied under supervisor Dorothy C. Wong and held a post at the University of Delhi (attested 2012).

Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned an MA at the Australian National University (attested 1983), studying under supervisors Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.
Ann Gleig is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under the doctoral supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal (attested 2010).

Ann Grodzins Gold is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned her BA, MA, and PhD in anthropology at the University of Chicago (~1970–1984). She held posts at Cornell University (~1988–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993).

Ann Heirman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held positions at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and served as a permanent member and director at Ghent University (2003–2012).

Ann Laura Stoler works in history and archaeology. Educated at Barnard College and Columbia University, she taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1983–1989) and University of Michigan (1989–2004), becoming Gründungsdirektorin at The New School in 2004.
Anna Andreeva is a scholar in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at Heidelberg University and Ghent University, where she is attested as a permanent member in 2026.

Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indologist who studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and Tübingen (MA, 1998). She served as Assistant Professor at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015) and later held a post at the University of Zurich (attested 2026).

Anna Balikci-Denjongpa is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed her PhD at SOAS under Lionel Caplan, studying also with traditional teachers. She served as Assistant Editor for Bulletin of Tibetology and Research Coordinator at Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (2002).

Anna Brown is a scholar of religious studies and a Zen student under Robert Kennedy (attested 2017). Attested in 2017, she served as chair of the political science department and director of the social justice program at Saint Peter's University.

Anna Filigenzi is an archaeology and Indology scholar. She joined the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East in 1984, directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003), and held posts at University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2012) and Federico II (2021).
Anna M. Shields is a Sinologist. She held academic posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and Princeton University (~2015).

Anna Sawerthal is a scholar of Tibetology. She earned an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and a PhD at Heidelberg University, having also studied under Johanna Buß, Dawa Tsering, and Norbu Tashi.

Anna Seidel was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied in Munich, Hamburg, and under Max Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein. She held posts at the EFEO (1969), Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1970–1991), and visited UH Mānoa and UCSB.

Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. She served at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (~1978–1990), UCLA (~1990–1999), and New York University (~1999).

Anna-Pya Sjödin is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed her PhD at Uppsala University in 2007. Her doctoral supervisors included Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, and she also studied under Barbro Eriksson.
Annarao Kulkarni works in computational Indology. He has held positions at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Anne Carolyn Klein is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Binghamton, Wisconsin-Madison, and Virginia (PhD), training under Jeffrey Hopkins and several Tibetan masters. She held posts at Harvard (~1984–1985) and Rice University (~1987), where she chaired religious studies.

Anne E. Monius was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She earned her undergraduate and graduate degrees at Harvard University, studying under Diana L. Eck and Kausalya Hart, and taught at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) and Harvard (from 2002).
